verdict.rationale: Ledgy lets admins create dedicated API service accounts that authenticate via the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant. The docs say these credentials are 'scoped per integration', tokens are short-lived (24h), and revocation is immediate, so per-agent credentials can be issued and killed. No permission-level scoping is documented, such as read-only access, per-operation or per-company limits, or role assignment for a service account, so least-privilege is only partly evidenced. Missing for 10: documented fine-grained permission scopes or roles for service accounts, least-privilege configuration options, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: the credentials are scoped per integration, the tokens are short-lived, and revocation takes effect immediately
Create one in the Ledgy app under Company Settings → General → API service accounts
Requests are authenticated with an OAuth 2.0 access token belonging to a service account.
Revoke deletes the service account and invalidates its outstanding access tokens right away.
